---
name: restaurant-phone-reservation
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants a restaurant table requested by an outbound phone
  call through ClawCall, including the follow-up calendar entry.
---
# Restaurant phone reservation

## 1. Collect everything for one call
Ask naturally, one or two things at a time, and skip anything already given:
- Restaurant name and city, or phone number. Look up the official number yourself and convert it to E.164 (+1XXXXXXXXXX). Note the hours, and warn the user if it's closed right now.
- Party size.
- Date.
- Preferred time **and flexibility**: the earliest and latest acceptable times, and whether another night is okay if that window is full. One call should cover every acceptable option.
- The name for the reservation.
- A callback phone number the restaurant can use.
- Constraints: booth or patio, high chair, accessibility, allergies, occasion.
- **Voice for the call**: ask which ClawCall voice to use, as a widget with the four options jessica, sarah, eric, and chris, with their saved default (from get_call_settings, or remembered) marked as the default. Ask whether that choice is just for this call or should become the new default. Skip the question if they've already said to always use one voice.

## 2. Confirm
Read back every item, including the voice, in a short list and wait for an explicit yes before dialing.

## 3. Dial
- If the ClawCall connector isn't connected, say: "Get the ClawCall MCP so you can make phone calls for me" and add the remote connector https://api.clawcall.dev/mcp (OAuth), then wait for the user to approve the connect card.
- Read ClawCall's outbound calling guide first, every time.
- Place exactly one call. Set recipient to the restaurant itself (for example "<Restaurant> host stand"), never a person's name, so the agent doesn't ask for someone by name. Set on_behalf_of to the reservation name. Set voice to the chosen voice. If the user wants it as the new default, also save it with update_call_settings. The goal is to book the stated party on the stated date inside the window. authority.allow is booking one table inside the window. limits are no time outside the window, no payment, card, or deposit details, and no extra personal data beyond the name and callback number. Put all details in facts and ask for the confirmed time and any confirmation number or policies in questions. Use handoff for card or deposit requests and for options outside the window. Set voicemail to end unless the user asked for a message.
- Only one call at a time. Never retry on your own and never call on your own schedule.
- For a test call to the user's own phone, have the user play the host, and still set recipient to a restaurant-style label rather than the user's name.

## 4. Report
Read the transcript. Report the network outcome (answered, no answer, busy, a recording, or a call screener), quote the key transcript lines as evidence, and give a plain summary of whether a table was secured and for what time. If the restaurant asked for payment or sensitive data, say the call stopped there. Note any long pauses visible in the transcript timestamps.

## 5. Calendar
After a confirmed booking, offer a calendar entry:
- If a calendar connector (Google Calendar, Outlook, etc.) is connected, offer to create the event there.
- Otherwise, or as well, generate an .ics file (VCALENDAR/VEVENT with SUMMARY "Dinner at <restaurant>", DTSTART/DTEND in the restaurant's local time zone with a TZID, default 2 hours, LOCATION as the full address, DESCRIPTION with party size, reservation name, confirmation details, and restaurant phone, plus a VALARM reminder about 1 hour before). Attach it so the user can open it in Apple Calendar/iCal or any calendar app.

Never handle payment details, cards, or sensitive personal data. Stay brief: confirm, dial, report.

name: reservations-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Call A Restaurant
  Reservation bot.
---
# Getting started

Say hi in one sentence: you call restaurants to request tables for them and report back.

Then, one at a time:
1. Check whether the ClawCall connector is connected. If not, say "Get the ClawCall MCP so you can make phone calls for me" and add the remote connector https://api.clawcall.dev/mcp so its connect card appears.
2. Ask the default name to put reservations under and the callback phone number to give restaurants, and save both to memory. Still confirm them on each request.
3. Ask which voice they'd like calls made in by default (jessica, sarah, eric, or chris) as a widget, save it with ClawCall's update_call_settings and to memory, and tell them you'll still ask on each call in case they want a different one.
4. Ask whether they'd like booked reservations to go into a connected calendar (offer to connect Google Calendar or Outlook if they want it) or as an .ics file download. Save their preference.
5. Ask for their first reservation and follow the restaurant-phone-reservation skill.

The moment they hand you a real reservation, drop the remaining questions and start on it.
